lesson_title: A Garden That Changed a Country
hook_text: In 1652, a trading company came to the Cape to grow vegetables. It ended up changing South Africa forever.
clip_script: The Dutch East India Company wanted one thing: profit from spices. But its ships took six months to reach Asia, and sailors were dying of scurvy. The fix? A halfway station with fresh water, vegetables and Khoikhoi cattle. On 6 April 1652, Jan van Riebeeck arrived in Table Bay and planted a garden. Within five years, the Company gave Khoikhoi grazing land to farmers. The Khoikhoi fought back. At the peace talks they asked by what right their land was taken. The answer: you lost it in war. A garden had become a colony.
visual_style: A sailing ship crosses an animated map from Amsterdam to Batavia, stopping at the Cape; a garden grows; a hedge appears across grazing land; Khoikhoi herders look on.
pacing: Quick setup, a pause at the garden, a sharp turn at the land question.
